answer: I would like to talk about a conversation that genuinely changed the direction of my life. A person who gave me really good advice was an uncle of mine, my father's younger brother, at a point when I was feeling completely lost about my future. It was just after I had finished my studies, and I was [[paralysed]] by the number of choices in front of me. Some friends were preparing for government jobs, others were going abroad, and I had no idea which way to turn. He sat me down one evening after dinner and told me something simple but profound: that it is better to try and fail than to spend your life wondering. What made his advice so valuable was that he spoke from experience, having left a safe job himself to try something new in his thirties. He encouraged me to stop overthinking and [[take the plunge]], even if the first step was a small one. That conversation was genuinely [[pivotal]], because it shifted me from fear to action. I ended up making a decision I had been putting off for months, and it turned out well: the following week I applied for a position at an education consultancy, and I have been working there ever since. Looking back, his words were exactly what I needed at that [[crucial]] moment. Honestly, I still repeat that advice to friends who find themselves stuck, and to nervous students too, because I have seen for myself how much difference it can make.

followUps.q: Do you usually take advice from other people?
followUps.answer: Yes, but I try to be selective. I listen to people who have real experience of the situation, and then I [[weigh up]] their views before deciding. In the end, the decision has to be mine.

followUps.q: Have you ever given someone advice that helped them?
followUps.answer: I hope so. In my job I advise students every day about universities and courses, and a few have come back to thank me, which is one of the most satisfying parts of the work.
